claims.text: A combined high-throughput DFT and machine-learning-augmented CALPHAD framework can accurately predict melting temperatures across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The framework can accurately predict fusion enthalpy and entropy across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The framework can accurately predict volume changes at melting across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The framework can accurately predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
High-throughput DFT can provide fundamental energetic and vibrational data for representative high-entropy-alloy compositions.
Machine learning can calibrate and extend CALPHAD assessments for extrapolation into less-sampled compositional spaces.
The approach is applicable under near-equilibrium conditions and moderate chemical disorder typical of many high-entropy alloys.
Accurate predictions require DFT to capture the key vibrational and electronic contributions to free energy.
Short-to-medium-range chemical ordering and local atomic interactions drive the solid-liquid free-energy difference.
DFT calculations provide atomic-level information such as interatomic potentials and vibrational spectra.
Calibrating DFT-derived information with experimental data through machine learning enables CALPHAD to predict the targeted thermodynamic properties.
Combining first-principles calculations with statistical learning refines property estimates over complex composition ranges.
Predicted melting temperatures will agree with precise experiments within ±20 K.
Predicted fusion enthalpies and entropies will agree with precise experiments within ±5%.
Predicted volume changes at melting will agree with precise experiments within ±1%.
Traditional CALPHAD models based only on experimental data and limited DFT input often fail to capture complex interactions in high-entropy alloys.
Extreme electronic correlation effects can reduce the reliability of the approach.
Predictions can become less reliable for compositions far outside the DFT training range.
Unforeseen atomic ordering or phase segregation can limit the applicability of the approach.
Exceeding any of the stated error limits for melting temperature, fusion enthalpy or entropy, or volume change at melting would falsify the proposed approach.

contradictions.description: The initial state describes elemental distributions as highly disordered, whereas the conditions restrict the approach to moderate chemical disorder; the intended disorder regime is therefore ambiguous.
